# Glaze

## Ingredients

- Six pounds of lean beef from the leg, or a knuckle of veal and beef to make six pounds
- Half a pound of lean ham, free from rind or smoky outside, scalded five minutes
- Three medium-sized onions with two cloves in each
- A turnip
- A carrot
- A small head of celery
- Five quarts of cold water
- Four quarts of hot water

## Instructions

1. Cut the meat into pieces two inches square or less.
2. Put the meat into a two-gallon pot with the onions, turnip, carrot, and celery.
3. Pour five quarts of cold water over the ingredients.
4. Let the mixture come slowly to the boiling-point, then skim it.
5. Draw the pot to a spot where it will gently simmer for six hours.
6. Strain the stock through a colander and return the meat and vegetables to the pot.
7. Add four quarts of hot water and let it boil for four hours longer.
8. Strain both stocks through a scalded cloth, heating them if they have cooled.
9. Put both stocks together into one large pot and boil as fast as possible with the cover off, using a large spoon to prevent boiling over and to stir occasionally.
10. When reduced to three pints, transfer to a small saucepan and boil more slowly.
11. Stir frequently with a wooden spoon until it thickens and has a fine yellowish-brown color, reducing to a quart or rather less.
12. Watch closely as it quickly burns.
13. When there is only a pint and a half, pour into small cups or jars, or dry in thin sheets by pouring into oiled tin pans an inch deep.
14. When cold, cut into two-inch squares and dry by exposure to the air until like glue.
15. If putting into pots, do not cover until all moisture has evaporated and the glaze shrinks from the sides.

## Notes

One square makes a cup of strong soup if dissolved in boiling water and seasoned. Salt must not be added for glaze.
